speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: IMOS is the textbook definition of a trap for a small account: a 98.7% max drawdown means a $100 stake could shrink to $1.30 before it ever recovers, and the 1.32 beta with only 0.34 correlation says it moves violently on its own clock, not the market's. The 14.6% pop today on 2.7x volume looks like a short squeeze, not fresh money, and RSI 77.7 warns the rubber band is stretched. With earnings not until 10 November, there is no catalyst to justify the chase; the risk of a 10-15% snap-back in a single session is real, and on a $100 position that loss is permanent capital impairment. Cash preserves the option to buy the next genuine setup.

speaker: Muse
text: Your $100 US / Rs10k India budget can’t realistically get an IPO allotment – US IPOs need hundreds per lot and Indian IPOs need a full lot worth far more than $10, and allotment is lottery-like so expected value is tiny after the lock-up. On Zerodha delivery for Reliance.NS the round-trip cost on Rs10,000 is about 0.38% ~Rs38 with zero brokerage, plus 20% short-term capital gains tax if you sell within 12 months or 12.5% long-term after the exemption, and you can only buy whole shares so price must be under Rs10k per share.
